log.headline: 56 points, +6 on the 50-point average. Overall rank 2,677,591.
notes: Vuskovic (0 Premier League minutes, behind Kadioglu, Struijk and Dunk at Brighton) replaced by Luke Shaw, who started all 38 last season.
Gvardiol (16 starts, heavily rotated) replaced by Marc Guehi (35 starts, 179 points) - same club, same fixture, far more certain minutes.
Net cost GBP 0.0m: the GBP 0.5m saved on Shaw paid for the Guehi upgrade exactly.
No chip played. Nothing to gain in GW1 and the bench is worth roughly 2 points on a Bench Boost.

RESULT: João Pedro 11 (goal, assist, 2 bonus), Guéhi 10 (goal, 2 bonus), Calafiori 9 (assist, clean sheet), Szoboszlai 8 (goal, 1 bonus). Haaland captained for 2 points, doubled to 4 — 90 minutes, 0.74 xG, no return.
7 points left on the bench, 6 of them Slater's (assist plus clean sheet at Hull) — the single biggest avoidable loss of the week.

The Guéhi swap paid off, but not for the reason given. He was advised on his Crystal Palace starts record, which was the wrong evidence. He delivered because Maresca is reportedly playing him in central midfield, a role change nobody predicted here.
The Shaw swap looks flat so far: 90 minutes, 1 point, 2 goals conceded — but the reasoning (guaranteed minutes over a player with none) still holds.

log.headline: 95 points, +14 on the 81-point average. Overall rank climbed 803,799 places to 1,873,792 - top 25%.
notes: Haaland delivered this time: 2 goals, 13 raw / 26 with the armband, at Crystal Palace. The GW1 blank really was fatigue, not lost form.

Bruno Fernandes had the bigger raw game (23 points - a hat-trick plus an assist, 3 bonus, at home to Ipswich under new manager Michael Carrick) than Haaland's 13. The captaincy call still went to Haaland on underlying + fixture logic and it worked, but Bruno's score shows the alternative case wasn't wrong, just lower-ceiling this particular week.
Guéhi reverted to orthodox centre-back (no repeat of the GW1 midfield cameo) in a 4-1 win over his old club Crystal Palace - 2 points, appearance only, no clean sheet, no goal involvement this time.
Calafiori (11: assist + clean sheet) and Raya (6: clean sheet) both delivered as Arsenal won away at Aston Villa without conceding.
Liverpool conceded twice at home to Forest: Virgil 1 point, Szoboszlai 4. Neither is an emergency after one bad defensive day, but both are now on the watch list.
Shaw played 72 minutes and returned only 2 points - the underlying weakness flagged pre-match (thin defensive-contribution numbers) played out as expected.
4 points left on the bench (down from 7 in GW1) - the Slater-to-front bench reorder advised last week worked.
No transfers made. 1 free transfer rolled into GW3 alongside a second - 2 FT banked, still no hits taken all season.

log.headline: Act: Shaw out, Egan in (frees £0.5m). Captain Haaland, comfortably - home to promoted Coventry, the softest fixture of any elite attacker in GW3.
notes: Shaw's underlying never recovered from the GW1-2 pattern flagged early: 0.00 xG and 0.28 xGI across 180 minutes, and the 9th-heaviest sell-off in the entire game today (-210,131 net). Egan (Hull, £4.0m paid) has 2 clean sheets in 2 starts and hasn't risen in price yet - bought ahead of a likely rise.

Virgil van Dijk shows similarly weak underlying (0 bonus, BPS 13, -172,052 net sold today) but gets a good fixture this week (Ipswich away, FDR2) - held one more week rather than sold on 2 games of data. Next name to go if he blanks again.
Guéhi confirmed back at centre-back for GW3 (Sports Mole, CityXtra, The Hard Tackle, all 2-3 Sept 2026) - the GW1 midfield cameo was a one-off, not an ongoing role change.

Bench order corrected: Will Hughes has 0 minutes in 2 games and is absent from Crystal Palace's own published GW3 lineup, so he drops behind Robbie van Ewijk (plays every week, just has a brutal fixture at Man City this week) - free to do, corrects an error from the GW2 build.
Both Wildcards, Free Hits, Bench Boosts and Triple Captains still available (2x each), first set expires at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan 2027).
COULD NOT VERIFY: the exact reason Will Hughes has played zero minutes all season (checked 3 Sept 2026).

corrections.what: Gvardiol -> Guehi advised on 35 starts vs 16
corrections.why_wrong: Those 35 starts were at Crystal Palace. Guehi had just moved to Man City where he must displace an established Gvardiol-Dias pairing. Old-club minutes are not evidence of new-club security.
corrections.fixed: Explicit STARTING RISK check added to the weekly routine prompt and CLAUDE.md.

corrections.why_wrong: Salah is no longer in the game and the API now lists Szoboszlai at penalties_order 1 and set-piece order 1. The note was right when written and is wrong now.
